chunks: “No servant draws near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with anything more beloved to Him than walking on foot to His Sacred House. Indeed, one hajj equals seventy hajj. And whoever walks apart from riding his camel, Allah records for him the reward of what lies between his walking and his riding. And when the pilgrim’s sandal strap breaks, Allah records for him the reward of what lies between his walking barefoot until he becomes shod.”

key_terms.الْحَجَّةَ الْوَاحِدَةَ: a single hajj performed in this virtuous manner
key_terms.الْمَشْيِ: walking on foot as an act of devotion during hajj
key_terms.بَيْتِهِ الْحَرَامِ: Allah’s Sacred House, the Ka'bah in Makkah

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for walking to hajj on foot in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the great merit of walking to the Sacred House of Allah for hajj, presenting it as an especially beloved act of قرب to Allah. It also highlights that hardship endured during pilgrimage, such as walking or going barefoot due to a broken sandal, is a cause for multiplied divine reward.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
"No servant draws closer to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, with anything more beloved to Him than walking to His Sacred House on foot. A single Hajj performed in this manner equals seventy Hajj. And whoever alternates between walking and riding their camel, Allah (swt) records for them the reward of both their walking and their riding.
If a pilgrim's sandal strap breaks, Allah (swt) records for them the reward for every step they take barefoot until they wear another sandal."
